source.extraction: accessible text layer of the official booklet PDF
source.pageNote: The accessible text layer did not preserve the booklet's pagination, so no entry carries an official page number. The booklet itself is identified by document reference and URL instead.

rights.note: These figures are original vector line art redrawn from the values and labels printed in the booklet. No pixel data from the official PDF is stored here. Whether a redraw of a published diagram may be reproduced is an open legal question recorded in docs/LICENSING.md and in ADR-0002; it is not resolved by this manifest.

entries.pageSource: official booklet; pagination not recoverable from the accessible text layer
entries.alt: Two graphs side by side. Left: x in metres against t in seconds, a straight line through the marked points (1 s, 1 m) and (2 s, 1.8 m). Right: y in metres against t in seconds, a parabola through the marked points (1 s, 1 m) and (2 s, 4 m).
entries.description: Two graphs side by side. The left graph plots x in metres against t in seconds and is a straight line passing through the marked points (1 s, 1 m) and (2 s, 1.8 m). The right graph plots y in metres against t in seconds and is a parabola passing through the marked points (1 s, 1 m) and (2 s, 4 m). The booklet prints these two pairs of coordinates as the table of values for the item.
entries.deviations: The two curves are drawn to the printed coordinate values rather than traced from the booklet's sketch, so the x-time line is exactly straight and the y-time curve is exactly a parabola.

entries.pageSource: official booklet; pagination not recoverable from the accessible text layer
entries.fidelity: topology determined from the printed states and the keyed options
entries.alt: Pressure against volume plot for an ideal gas. State A lies at pressure 3P, state B at pressure 2P and state C at pressure P; B and C share the same volume, so they sit on one vertical line. A curve runs from A down to B and a steeper curve runs from A down to C.
entries.description: A pressure against volume plot with three states. State A lies at pressure 3P and a smaller volume; state B lies at pressure 2P and state C at pressure P, and B and C share the same volume, so they sit on one vertical line. A curve runs from A down to B, labelled as the isothermal path BA, and a steeper curve runs from A down to C, labelled as the adiabatic path CA.
entries.deviations: The arrangement of the three states is derived rather than traced: the booklet's text layer preserved only the labels 3P, 2P and P and the names of the paths. This is the single arrangement of those pressures that leaves BA isothermal and CA adiabatic at the same time.

entries.fidelity: element labels reproduced; wiring determined from the keyed options
entries.alt: A rectangular circuit. The left branch holds a 12 volt battery; the top wire runs from it through a 500 ohm resistor to a junction. From that junction a vertical branch carries a resistor R down to the bottom rail, and the top wire continues right through a galvanometer G to the right-hand branch, which holds a 2 volt cell.
entries.description: A rectangular circuit. The left branch contains a 12 volt battery whose positive plate is on top; its top wire runs through a 500 ohm resistor to a junction. From that junction a vertical branch carries a resistor R down to the bottom rail, and the top wire continues right through a galvanometer G to the right-hand branch, which contains a 2 volt cell whose positive plate is on top, before returning along the bottom rail to the battery.
entries.deviations: The wiring is derived from the printed element labels and the shape of the circuit the item describes. The booklet's text layer preserved the labels 500 ohm, G, 12 V, R and 2 V but not the connections between them. The cell polarities are drawn with the positive plate uppermost, which is the polarity the labels are read with.

entries.pageSource: official booklet; pagination not recoverable from the accessible text layer
entries.alt: Graph of power P against load resistance R. A curve rises from the origin, reaches its highest point at M, and then falls away towards the horizontal axis. M stands above the load resistance marked r on the horizontal axis, and the vertical axis carries the mark E squared over r.
entries.description: A graph of power P on the vertical axis against load resistance R on the horizontal axis. A curve rises from the origin, reaches its highest point at the point M, and then falls away towards the horizontal axis. The point M stands above the load resistance marked r on the horizontal axis, and the vertical axis carries the mark E squared over r. The peak of the curve is one quarter of the way up the marked E squared over r level.
entries.deviations: The curve is drawn from the formula rather than traced, so its shape is exact. The peak is placed at one quarter of the marked E squared over r level, which is what makes the printed coordinate options meaningful.

entries.fidelity: wiring reconstructed from the stem text and the keyed options
entries.alt: A circuit with two vertical branches joined by a top wire and a bottom wire. The capacitor C sits in the top wire. The left branch holds a supply of emf E and a switch S1. The right branch holds a resistor R and a switch S2. Both switches are drawn open.
entries.description: A circuit with two vertical branches joined by a top wire and a bottom wire. The capacitor C sits in the top wire. The left branch holds a supply of emf E and a switch S1. The right branch holds a resistor R and a switch S2, and the two branches share the bottom wire. Both switches are drawn open.
entries.deviations: The booklet's text layer carried no labels for this figure at all, so the wiring is reconstructed from the stem text, which names a capacitor, a supply of emf E, a switch and a resistor R, and from the shape of the item. The labels S1 and S2 on the two switches, and the note that S2 is the switch closed at t = t0, are editorial: the booklet says only that the switch is closed at t = t0. This entry is marked for owner review of the original page.

entries.fidelity: geometry reproduced to the printed labels
entries.alt: Young's double slit experiment with white light. A white light source on the left shines on a vertical barrier carrying two slits, S1 above and S2 below, separated by a distance b. A vertical screen stands to the right at a distance d from the slits. A point P on the screen lies directly in front of S1. A ray is drawn from S1 to P and a second ray from S2 to P, and a dashed line marks the central axis midway between the slits.
entries.description: A white light source on the left shines on a vertical barrier carrying two slits, S1 above and S2 below, separated by a distance b. A vertical screen stands to the right at a distance d from the slits. A point P on the screen lies directly in front of S1. A ray is drawn from S1 to P and a second ray from S2 to P, and a dashed line marks the central axis midway between the two slits.
entries.deviations: The booklet's text layer preserved the labels S1, S2, P, screen, b and d but not the artwork. The barrier, the screen, the rays and the central axis are redrawn from the stem text, which states that d is much greater than b.

entries.fidelity: chain order preserved; one dropped methyl label restored
entries.alt: The structural formula of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane. A central carbon is joined on the left to a methyl group, above to a methyl group, below to a further methyl group and on the right to a CH2 group. The CH2 group is joined to a CH group, which carries a methyl group below it and is joined on the right to a terminal methyl group.
entries.description: The structural formula of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane. A central carbon is joined on the left to a methyl group, above to a methyl group, below to a further methyl group and on the right to a CH2 group. The CH2 group is joined to a CH group, which carries a methyl group below it and is joined on the right to a terminal methyl group.
entries.deviations: The booklet's text layer preserved the chain order of the structural formula, a quaternary carbon followed by CH2, then CH, then CH3, but dropped one methyl label. The redraw restores the two methyl groups drawn below the quaternary carbon and the CH group, which is the only arrangement consistent with the printed skeleton and with the board's key. This entry is marked for owner review of the original page.

entries.alt: On the left, a current source marked i(t) drives a single loop made of a 3 ohm resistor, a 2 millihenry inductor and a 500 microfarad capacitor in series. On the right, a graph of the source current i(t) against time in milliseconds: the current is a straight-line triangle that starts at minus 5 amperes at 0 milliseconds, rises to plus 5 amperes at 3 milliseconds and falls back to minus 5 amperes at 6 milliseconds.
entries.description: On the left, a current source marked i(t) drives a single loop made of a 3 ohm resistor, a 2 millihenry inductor and a 500 microfarad capacitor in series. On the right, a graph of the source current i(t) against time in milliseconds: the current is a straight-line triangle that starts at minus 5 amperes at 0 milliseconds, rises to plus 5 amperes at 3 milliseconds and falls back to minus 5 amperes at 6 milliseconds.
entries.deviations: The waveform is drawn as the straight-sided triangle the printed axis labels describe. The largest current is 5 amperes, which is what fixes the scale of the plot.

entries.description: A 5 volt supply at the bottom of the circuit feeds two capacitors in series along the top wire. The left capacitor is C1 with a capacitance of 5 microfarads and the voltage drop V1 across it; the right capacitor is C2 with a capacitance of 10 microfarads and the voltage drop V2 across it.
entries.deviations: The printed values C1 = 5 microfarad, C2 = 10 microfarad and a 5 volt supply are reproduced. The polarity of the supply is not stated in the booklet's text layer and is not marked in the drawing.

entries.description: Three vertical branches connect a top rail to a bottom rail. The left branch holds a 50 volt source in series with a 5 ohm resistor, the middle branch a 40 volt source in series with a 4 ohm resistor, and the right branch a 30 volt source in series with a 3 ohm resistor. entries.deviations: The booklet's text layer carried the element labels 50 V, 40 V, 30 V, 5 ohm, 4 ohm, 3 ohm and 2 ohm but not the wiring. The arrangement drawn here is the one that puts every printed element to work. It is marked for owner review of the original page, and the board voided the item in any case.
